title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow?

items.stem: Which statement best tells a workflow apart from an agent?

options.text: A workflow can use tools, but an agent only answers from training
A workflow calls the model once, but an agent calls it many times
In a workflow, code fixes the steps in advance; in an agent, the model chooses them
A workflow runs without any model, but an agent always needs one

items.stem: A makerspace assistant is built like this. Step 1: the model reads the student's message and labels it either "manual question" or "booking request". Step 2: the program's code checks the label. For a manual question it runs a page search and asks the model to answer from the page; for a booking request it calls the calendar tool and asks the model to write a reply. Who owns the control flow here, and what is this system?

options.text: The code owns it, so this is a workflow; the model only labels the message
The model owns it, so this is an agent; it decides which branch runs
The model owns it, so this is an agent; it is called more than once
The code owns it, so this is an agent; it has tools and branches

items.stem: The team has a model budget of $20 for the semester, and every model call costs $0.01. A fixed workflow answers a request with exactly 2 model calls. An agent needs an average of 5 model calls per request, because it decides its own steps. How many more requests can the $20 budget cover with the workflow than with the agent?

Booking a machine always follows the same three steps: check the calendar, confirm the slot with the student, then write the booking. In one sentence, why is a fixed workflow a better choice than an agent for this task?
Which of these makerspace tasks is the best candidate for an agent, rather than a fixed workflow?

options.text: Emailing each student a reminder 24 hours before their booking
Planning how to make a part from a vague description, using whichever manuals and machines it needs
Writing each new booking into the shared spreadsheet in the same format
Telling a student which of three fixed training levels they have reached

items.stem: At a design review, a teammate proposes making the whole assistant one agent, "because agents are the more advanced option". Which reply is best?

options.text: Agree: an agent can do anything a workflow does at the same cost
Agree: only an agent can call tools such as the calendar
Disagree: an agent cannot be trusted to call any tool at all
Disagree: use fixed workflows for known steps, and an agent only where steps cannot be known
